families.title: Probabilistic programs: Dice, Alea.jl, Roulette and further systems
families.intro: The programs of the Dice, Alea.jl, Roulette and Geni papers, against Dice, Alea.jl and Roulette, and on the programs they take Geni, noDice, Psi, Genfer, SPPL, Pluck, PITA, aspmc, Storm, PRISM, Ace, Merlin, pyAgrum, pgmpy, libDAI and TensorInference.jl. tddlog runs its own encoding of a program's integers (binary, never one-hot) and is asked what the baseline answers: single marginals where the baseline gives single marginals, a distribution's values only where it computes them. Alea.jl's times leave out Julia's start-up and compilation, as its papers time it; the dashed lines add them, and Racket's start-up to Roulette's.

setup: Three machines: a cloud machine with 96 physical cores and 1488 GB of memory, for the Alea.jl and noDice programs and the bit-blasted programs; a cloud machine with 96 physical cores and 1488 GB of memory, for the Dice paper's programs and Geni's programs and Roulette's programs; and a lab machine with 16 physical cores and 125 GB of memory, for the earlier run of Dice, ProbLog's references and the samplers on the bit-blasted programs. A run is one job that holds its machine alone. Programs run as independent jobs in lanes, each pinned to one logical CPU on its own physical core, with the machine's memory split between the lanes. In a lane all systems run on an instance back to back, in an order rotated by instance and repetition, so that the systems share the lanes alike.

The release run, all of its parts at one version of tddlog, each part with all of its systems in the same lanes: the arithmetic, sequence and noDice programs (60 lanes, 24 GB a process, three repetitions, 600 s, on the machine with 96 physical cores and 1488 GB of memory, 2026-10-19); the networks, the Dice paper's programs and the loop programs (94 lanes, 15 GB a process, three repetitions, 300 s for the networks and the Dice paper's programs and 600 s for the loop programs, on the machine with 96 physical cores and 1488 GB of memory, 2026-10-19); Roulette's programs (52 lanes, 28 GB a process, three repetitions, 600 s, on the machine with 96 physical cores and 1488 GB of memory, 2026-10-19); the bit-blasted programs for tddlog and Alea.jl (45 lanes, 33 GB a process, three repetitions, 600 s, on the machine with 96 physical cores and 1488 GB of memory, 2026-10-19); and Geni's programs, with ProbLog's d-DNNF timed beside the others (49 lanes, 30 GB a process, three repetitions, 600 s, on the machine with 96 physical cores and 1488 GB of memory, 2026-10-19). Dice, ProbLog's references and the samplers on the bit-blasted programs come from an earlier run (5 lanes, 25 GB a process, three repetitions, 600 s, 2026-10-12) on the same circuits; neither those systems nor the circuits have changed since. Times compare within a run: on the bit-blasted programs the plots show tddlog and Alea.jl, and Dice's times are in the tables only. The plots of all programs put the runs together.

A program with a size runs from small to large, and a system that fails on one size (a timeout, out of memory, a crash) is not run on the larger sizes of that program; the tables mark those `skipped`, and they count as failures.
A time is the median of the repetitions, a failed repetition counted as longer than any time: of three repetitions, a system must answer in two.

For tddlog and Dice, the wall time of the process: parsing, compiling and answering every query. For Alea.jl, the time the program reports for building the model and computing its answers a second time in the same process, without Julia's compilation, as the papers time it; the process's wall time, with Julia's start-up, loading Alea.jl and compiling its methods, is the dashed line in the plots and the "process" column in the tables. For Roulette, the time the artifact's own `time` reports for building and querying the program; the dashed line adds Racket's start-up and loading.
